<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|212|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XXIIII.}}</noinclude>him, saying, Tarie vvith vs, because it is tovvard night, and the day is novv farre spent. And he vvent in vvith them. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=30}}† And it came to passe, vvhiles he sate at the table vvith them, he {{sup|‖}} tooke bread, and blessed and brake, and did reach to them. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=31}}† And their eies vvere opened, and they knevv him: and he vanished out of their sight. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=32}}† And they said one to the other, VVas not our hart burning in vs, vvhiles he spake in the vvay, and opened vnto vs the scriptures? {{verse|chapter=24|verse=33}}† And rising vp the same houre they vvent backe into Hierusalem: and they found the eleuen gathered together, and those that vvere vvith them, {{verse|chapter=24|verse=34}}† saying, That our Lord is risen in deede, and hath appeared to Simon. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=35}}† And they told the things that vvere done in the vvay: and hovv they knevv him in the breaking of bread.⊣

{{verse|chapter=24|verse=36}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 16, 14. Io. 20, 19.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Gospel vpō Tuesday in Easter weeke.}}∷ And vvhiles they speake these things, {{sc|Iesvs}} stoode in the middes of them, and he saith to them, Peace be to you: it is I. feare not. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=37}}† But they being troubled and frighted, imagined that they savv a spirit. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=38}}† And he said to them, VVhy are you troubled, and cogitations arise into your harts? {{verse|chapter=24|verse=39}}† See my handes, and feete, that it is I my self. handle, and see: for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as you see me to haue. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=40}}† And vvhen he had said this, he shevved them his handes and feete. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=41}}† But they yet not beleeuing and marueiling for ioy, he said, Haue you here any thing to be eaten? {{verse|chapter=24|verse=42}}† But they offred him a peece of fish broiled, and a honie combe. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=43}}† And vvhen he had eaten before them, taking the remaines he gaue to them.

{{verse|chapter=24|verse=44}}† And he said to them, These are the vvordes vvhich I spake to you, vvhen I vvas yet vvith you, that al things must needes be fulfilled, vvhich are vvritten in the lavv of Moyses, and the Prophets, and the Psalmes, of me. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=45}}† Then he opened their vnderstanding, that they might vnderstand the Scriptures. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=46}}† and he said to them, That so it is vvritten, and so it behoued Christ to suffer, and to rise againe from the dead the third day: {{verse|chapter=24|verse=47}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ As he shal be Anathema (saith S. Aug.) which preacheth that Christ neither suffered nor rose againe, because we learne by the Gospel, ''That it behoued Christ to suffer and to rise againe the third day:'' so he shal also be Anathema, whosoeuer preacheth the Church to be}}∷ and {{sup|‖}} penance to be preached in his name and remission of sinnes vnto al nations, ⊣ beginning from Hierusalem. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=48}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 1, 8. 2, 1.''}}* And you are vvitnesses of these things. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=49}}† And I send the promes of my Father vpon you: but you, tarie in the citie, til you be endued vvith povver from high.

{{verse|chapter=24|verse=50}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ASCENSION DAY.}}∷ And he brought them forth abrode into Bethánia: and lifting vp his handes he {{sup|‖}} blessed them. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=51}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 16, 19. Act. 1, 9.''}}* And it came to passe, vvhiles he blessed them, he departed from them, and<noinclude>{{rh|||vvas}}</noinclude>
